Title: Aerial World Model for Long-horizon Visual Generation and Navigation in 3D Space (ANWM)
Authors: Weichen Zhang, Peizhi Tang, Xin Zeng, Fanhang Man, Shiquan Yu, Zichao Dai, Baining Zhao, Hongjin Chen, Yu Shang, Wei Wu, Chen Gao, Xinlei Chen, Xin Wang, Yong Li, Wenwu Zhu
What they did: Action-conditioned CDiT aerial world model trained on ~350k Unreal Engine segments; ranks candidate trajectories by their imagined final frame. Actions are 4-DoF (dx, dy, dz, dyaw); pitch and roll are ignored. Scored with LPIPS, DreamSim, FID only.

Title: AirScape: An Aerial Generative World Model with Motion Controllability
Authors: Baining Zhao, Rongze Tang, Mingyuan Jia, Ziyou Wang, Fanghang Man, Xin Zhang, Yu Shang, Weichen Zhang, Chen Gao, Wei Wu, Xin Wang, Xinlei Chen, Yong Li
What they did: Aerial generative world model with motion controllability, built from real aerial video. No physics check reported.

Title: Captain Safari: A World Engine with Pose-Aligned 3D Memory
Authors: Yu-Cheng Chou, Xingrui Wang, Yitong Li, Jiahao Wang, Hanting Liu, Cihang Xie, Alan Yuille, Junfei Xiao
Institution: Johns Hopkins University; Tsinghua University; UC Santa Cruz
What they did: World engine for long, 3D-consistent video under aggressive 6-DoF camera motion, using pose-aligned 3D memory; introduces the OpenSafari camera-controlled UAV video set.

Title: MotionScape: A Motion-Stratified UAV Video Benchmark for World Modeling and Future Video Generation
Authors: Zile Guo, Zhan Chen, Xiaoxuan Liu, Enze Zhu, Kan Wei, Yongkang Zou, Sijia Ma, Lei Wang
Institution: Aerospace Information Research Institute, CAS; University of CAS; Xi'an Surveying & Mapping Institute
What they did: 228 real FPV/UAV YouTube clips, stratified by motion; benchmarks Cosmos-Predict2.5, Wan2.2, CogVideoX, LongCat and MAGI-1 on Image2World and Video2World protocols. Metrics are PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS/FVD/CLIPSim only.

Title: AeroAct: Action-Centered World-Action Models for Language-Conditioned Quadrotor Flight
Authors: Xinhong Zhang, Qiyuan Zhu, Yubo Huang, Haolin Chen, Runqing Wang, Yuhao Mo, Zhongxin Chen, Yu Hu, Xinjiang Wang, Jian Sun, Gang Wang
What they did: Wan2.1-1.3B world-action model predicting 5th-order trajectory chunks; first real quadrotor flight with a world-action model. Feasibility is enforced on the action side (via DiffAero), not checked on generated video.

Title: Aero-World: Action-Conditioned Aerial Video Generation from Inertial Controls
Authors: Abdul Mohaimen Al Radi, Kunyang Li, Yuzhang Shang, Mubarak Shah, Yu Tian
What they did: Action-conditioned aerial video generation driven by inertial controls. New find, not in your review: it conditions on inertial signals, so it is directly relevant to tilt-vs-acceleration.

Title: Uncertainty-Aware World Model for Aerial Image-Goal Navigation
Authors: Deyi Zhu, Haoyu Fan, Yinan Zhu, Weichen Zhang, Shilin Ma, Xinlei Chen, Yansong Tang
Institution: Tsinghua Shenzhen International Graduate School, Tsinghua University
What they did: Image-goal aerial navigation that ranks candidate trajectories by predicted views with uncertainty estimates.

Title: Skytopia: Monocular Drone Navigation with Action-Conditioned Latent World Models
Authors: Yuhang Zhang, Rangya Zhang, Yujing Shang, Zhuoyuan Yu, Weiying Wang, Steven Yang, Qingsong Yan, Chao Yan, Mir Feroskhan
Institution: Nanyang Technological University; Autel US; XGRIDS
What they did: Monocular drone navigation using action-conditioned latent world models. Latent, not pixel-level; no physics check.

Title: DroneWAM: Efficient World Action Model for Drone Visual Navigation
Authors: Liang Yao, Fan Liu, Hongbo Lu, Wei Xu, Jianyu Jiang, Yijun Shen, Chuanyi Zhang, Pai Peng
Institution: Hohai University; Shanghai Jiao Tong University; Nanjing University; Southeast University; East China Normal University; CowaRobot
What they did: Efficient world-action model for drone visual navigation; anticipates how candidate actions change future observations.

Title: ForeFly: A Dual-Horizon World Action Model for Aerial Vision-Language Navigation
Authors: Kunhui Wang, Xintong Zhang, Junyu Gao, Changsheng Xu
Institution: CAS Institute of Automation; UCAS; Duke Kunshan University; Peng Cheng Laboratory
What they did: Dual-horizon world-action model for aerial vision-language navigation over long trajectories.

Title: DiffWAM: A Fast and Efficient Navigation World Action Model
Authors: Mo Zhu, Yuze Wu, Xijie Huang, Xiao Cui, Fei Gao, Xin Zhou
What they did: Navigation world-action model that converts video-foundation-model priors into UAV motion without expensive future-video synthesis.

Title: WorldFly: A World-Model-Based Vision-Language-Action Model for UAV Navigation
Authors: Shengtao Zheng, Kai Li, Weichen Zhang, Yu Meng, Chen Gao, Xinlei Chen, Yong Li, Xiao-Ping Zhang
Institution: Tsinghua Shenzhen International Graduate School; BNRist; Tsinghua University
What they did: World-model-based VLA for UAV navigation. New find, not in your review.

Title: ImagineUAV: Aerial Vision-Language Navigation via World-Action Modeling and Kinodynamic Planning
Authors: Xuchen Liu, Jiawei Huang, Shihao Xia, Bingxi Liu, Jinqiang Cui, Jiankun Yang
Institution: Pengcheng Laboratory; Guangzhou University; Southern University of Science and Technology
What they did: Grounds free-form instructions into 6-DoF flight with world-action modeling plus kinodynamic planning. New find, not in your review: it brings dynamics in on the planning side.

Title: VehDyn: A Driving World Model Benchmark for Vehicle Dynamics
Authors: Tianyi Wang, Wangsheng Du, Jiazhou Chen, Tianyi Zeng, Xiangyu Li, Jiseop Byeon, Yujin Wang, Yiming Xu, Yangyang Wang, Bingzhao Gao, Sikai Chen, Zhaomiao Guo, Junfeng Jiao, Christian Claudel, Alexandre Bayen
Institution: UT Austin; UC Berkeley (inferred from author list, verify)
Venue: Preprint (dataset to be released after acceptance)
What they did: CARLA-CarSim benchmark (10,080 configurations). Recovers 6-DoF ego state from generated video with DPVO, then scores trajectory, kinematics and dynamics (friction-circle constraint). 12 models benchmarked; visual quality and dynamics rank correlate at only rho = 0.39.

Title: KineBench: Benchmarking Embodied World Models via IDM-Free Kinematic Grounding
Authors: Zeyu Liu, Zhangzhe Zhu, Yang Zhang, Chenyou Fan, Chenjia Bai, Xuelong Li
Institution: TeleAI (China Telecom); NUS; Fudan University; Tsinghua University; NWPU Shenzhen Research Institute
What they did: Replaces learned inverse-dynamics models with a chain of frozen models to extract 6-DoF pose from generated manipulation video, so extraction error is measurable and failures can be attributed to the world model.

Title: What About Gravity in Video Generation? Post-Training Newton's Laws with Verifiable Rewards
Authors: M. Q. Le, Y. Zhu, V. Kalogeiton, D. Samaras (initials as cited by KineBench)
What they did: Uses RAFT optical flow as a velocity proxy and a constant-acceleration residual as a verifiable post-training reward. Residual-only rewards get hacked (the model freezes motion). Author first names are from a citation list, so verify them.

Title: DriveReferee: Geometric Safety Verdicts Need Not Be Learned for Driving World-Action Models
Authors: Fengcheng Yu, Dhruv Parikh, Junjie Ye, Maulik Bhatt, Thang Vu, Igor Vasiljevic, Vitor Guizilini, Yue Wang
Institution: University of Southern California; Woven by Toyota; Toyota Research Institute
What they did: A zero-parameter analytic rule on predicted scene state matches or beats a learned verifier trained on 66,385 labels. Source of the framing 'learn perception, compute the verdict'.

Title: Validate the Dream Before You Trust Its Verdict: Admissibility for World-Model Simulators
Authors: Christian Oefinger, Finn Rasmus Schäfer, Korbinian Moller, Mattia Piccinini, Johannes Betz
Institution: Technical University of Munich (Autonomous Vehicle Systems Lab)
What they did: Proposes an admissibility ladder (L0 looks plausible through L4 verdicts transfer to reality) for trusting world-model simulators. Positions a dynamics verifier as an L2/L3 instrument.

Title: PVBench: Quantifying Physical Plausibility in Video Generation with Object-Level Physical Measurements
Authors: Kaiwei Chen, Moran Li, Zhenye Gan, Yabiao Wang, Chengjie Wang, Kexin Zhang, Yong Liu, Jiangning Zhang
Institution: Zhejiang University (APRIL Lab); Huazhong University of Science and Technology; Tencent Youtu Lab
What they did: Measures physical plausibility of generated video from object-level physical measurements rather than a VLM opinion.

Title: Principia: Relational Physics Tests for Video Models
Authors: Varun Varma Thozhiyoor, Shivam Tripathi, Venkatesh Babu Radhakrishnan, Anand Bhattad
Institution: Indian Institute of Science; Johns Hopkins University
What they did: Relational physics tests that avoid dependence on frame rate, object scale and camera calibration, which are often ambiguous in generated video.

Title: PhyProbe: Rethinking Physical Consistency Evaluation in Generated Videos
Authors: Max Ku, Jiaojiao Fan, Zekun Hao, Francesco Ferroni, Heng Wang, Wenhu Chen, Ming-Yu Liu, Prithvijit Chattopadhyay
Institution: NVIDIA; University of Waterloo; Vector Institute
What they did: Argues off-the-shelf VLM judges are myopic to physical dynamics and proposes a different consistency evaluation.

Title: PhysTrace: Interpretable Temporal Evaluation of Physical Consistency in Video Generative Models
Authors: Taekoan Yoo, Wonkyung Jung, Kyunghun Kim, Kyeongbo Kong
What they did: Temporal, interpretable evaluation of physical consistency in video generators, motivated by world-action models relying on pretrained video models.

Title: PIVOT: Physics-Grounded Verification for AI-Generated Audio-Video Detection
Authors: Bo Zheng, Kangran Zhao, Xiaoyu Zhang, Weinan Guan, Zhiheng Li, Yize Chen, Haizhou Li, Baoyuan Wu, Qingshan Liu, Siwei Lyu
Institution: CUHK Shenzhen; Nanjing University of Posts and Telecommunications; University at Buffalo
What they did: Detects AI-generated audio-video with physics-grounded consistency checks. The same kind of test as ours, seen from a forensics angle.

Title: WorldOracle: Benchmarking Action-Conditioned World Models against Real-World Executions
Authors: Haoyi Duan, Liliang Chen, Nan Wang, Yang Zhang, Yuhang Lu, Xiaotong Chen, Wei-Cheng Tseng, Shenyuan Gao, Zhaoshuo Li, Jingyi Jin, Pooya Jannaty, Dhruv Shah, Yuke Zhu, Ming-Yu Liu, Maoqing Yao, Guanghui Ren
Institution: AgiBot; NVIDIA; Princeton University; UT Austin; University of Toronto
What they did: Benchmarks action-conditioned world models against paired real-world executions.

Title: WMEval: Evaluating Interactive World Models Grounded on Physical Simulations
Authors: Lanxiang Hu, Yixin Huang, Abhilash Shankarampeta, Zilin Dai, Yuyuan Wu, Kun Qian, Junze Liu, Arvind Srinivasan, Mingjia Huo, Will Lin, Kai Zhong, Weiqi Zhang, Tian Wang, Qingjun Cui, Tajana Rosing, Hao Zhang
What they did: Evaluates interactive world models against physical simulation rather than perceptual similarity.

Title: World Models' Last Exam in Physics
Authors: Mingju Gao, Qingle Liu, Yuzhao Peng, Xinjie Lin, Ziming Qin, Zheng Jiang, Wenyi Li, Calvin Xiao, Youjie Zheng, Kaisen Yang, Qinhuai Na
What they did: Physics benchmark for video world models that look convincing but are physically inconsistent.

Title: GAUGE: A Measurement-Grounded Benchmark for Physical Fidelity in Simulation Engines and Video World Models
Authors: Shuai Wang, Yaxin Feng, Xuekun Jiang, Shihan Tian, Ningyu Yan, Xing Shen, Chaoyang Lyu, Hui Wang, Yunsong Zhou, Hanqing Wang, Jiangmiao Pang, Yang Xiang, Xing Gao, Chunhua Shen, Weinan Zhang
Institution: Shanghai AI Laboratory; HKUST; Shanghai Jiao Tong University; Zhejiang University
What they did: Measurement-grounded benchmark comparing physical fidelity of simulation engines and video world models.

Title: World Embedding Benchmark
Authors: Yiqi Liu, Ruifeng Yuan, Yang Wang, Long Li, Fengyu Cai, Hou Pong Chan, Jialin Yu, Hao Zhang, Chenghua Lin, Chenghao Xiao
Institution: World-Embedding Team (affiliations not on first page; verify)
What they did: Probes how video representations encode physical information.

Title: Does Physics Live in the Activations? Localizing Physical Quantities in Video Diffusion Models
Authors: Jonas Kneifl, Jakub Skalski, Bartłomiej Twardowski, Kamil Deja
Institution: IDEAS Research Institute (Warsaw); Computer Vision Center, UAB; Warsaw University of Technology
What they did: Probes video diffusion activations for where physical quantities are encoded.

Title: GEOPHYS: The Geometry of Physical Plausibility
Authors: Christian Internò, Alexander Pondaven, Habon Issa, Fabio Pizzati, Francesco Pinto, Markus Olhofer, Ivan Laptev, Philip Torr, Eero P. Simoncelli, Barbara Hammer, David Klindt
Institution: Bielefeld University; University of Oxford; Cold Spring Harbor Laboratory; MBZUAI; Honda Research Institute EU; NYU; Flatiron Institute
What they did: Training-free plausibility score from the geometry of per-frame features of frozen image encoders (speed, curvature, acceleration, linear-prediction residual). Detects physics violations on LikePhys and IntPhys2, and works as a best-of-N verifier on PhysicsIQ. Time-symmetric, so it cannot see time-direction violations. Relevant as a cheap learned-score baseline.

Title: PhyMetric: Diagnosing Physical Plausibility in Text-to-Video Generation via Scene-Level QA
Authors: Siwei Meng, Xuerou Cai, Rui Hu, Ping Liu
What they did: Diagnoses physical plausibility of text-to-video outputs with scene-level yes/no questions answered by a VLM judge, using 1,115 scenes over 50 physical categories (from the abstract).

Title: Physics Question Scene Graph: Fine-grained Evaluation of Physical Plausibility in Text-to-Video Generation
Authors: Atin Pothiraj, Jaemin Cho, Yue Zhang, Elias Stengel-Eskin, Mohit Bansal
Institution: UNC Chapel Hill; AI2; Johns Hopkins University; UT Austin
What they did: Question-scene-graph judge: a VLM writes object, action and physics yes/no questions with dependencies and answers them on the video (FinePhyEval, 260 videos). VLM answers on physics questions are weakest (about 65% for GPT-5.5). A VLM-judge baseline for us.

Title: VideoPhy: Evaluating Physical Commonsense for Video Generation
Authors: Hritik Bansal, Zongyu Lin, Tianyi Xie, Zhenghao Zong, Michal Yarom, Yonatan Bitton, Chenfanfu Jiang, Yizhou Sun, Kai-Wei Chang, Aditya Grover
What they did: Benchmark and automatic evaluator of physical commonsense in generated video.

Title: World-in-World: World Models in a Closed-Loop World
Authors: Jiahan Zhang, Muqing Jiang, Nanru Dai, Taiming Lu, Arda Uzunoglu, Shunchi Zhang, Yana Wei, Jiahao Wang, Vishal M. Patel, Paul Pu Liang et al.
What they did: Closed-loop evaluation of world models by reading actions out of video with learned inverse dynamics. Found visual realism largely uncorrelated with physical understanding (as cited by VehDyn).

Title: WoW, wo, val! A Comprehensive Embodied World Model Evaluation Turing Test
Authors: Chun-Kai Fan, Xiaowei Chi, Xiaozhu Ju et al.
Institution: Peking University; Beijing Innovation Center of Humanoid Robotics; HKUST
What they did: Embodied world-model evaluation with an 'IDM Turing test' (as cited by VehDyn).

Title: ACT-Bench: Towards Action Controllable World Models for Autonomous Driving
Authors: Hidehisa Arai, Keishi Ishihara, Tsubasa Takahashi, Yu Yamaguchi
What they did: Scores action-following by recovering the ego trajectory from generated video with monocular visual odometry (ADE, FDE, action-match rate).

Title: Do Robotic World Models Really Follow Actions? Diagnosing and Aligning Action-Conditioned Generation for Policy Learning
Authors: Sixiang Chen, Jiaming Liu, Jixian Wu, Yichen Guo, Tinghao Wang, Siyuan Qian, Hao Chen, Jiajun Cao, Jian Tang, Shanghang Zhang
Institution: Peking University; Beijing Innovation Center of Humanoid Robotics; NYU; UESTC; NTU; CUHK
What they did: Finds that generated futures often do not reflect the commanded action, and proposes diagnosing and aligning action-conditioned generation for policy learning.

Title: Minimum Snap Trajectory Generation and Control for Quadrotors
Authors: Daniel Mellinger, Vijay Kumar
What they did: Shows quadrotor dynamics are differentially flat in position and yaw, so the trajectory fixes thrust direction (roll and pitch) at every instant. Foundation for the implied-tilt equation.

Title: Differential Flatness of Quadrotor Dynamics Subject to Rotor Drag for Accurate Tracking of High-Speed Trajectories
Authors: Matthias Faessler, Antonio Franchi, Davide Scaramuzza
Institution: University of Zurich; ETH Zurich; LAAS-CNRS (Université de Toulouse)
What they did: Extends flatness to include linear rotor drag, so steady-speed flight still tilts. Source for the drag term k_d.

Title: Deep Patch Visual Odometry
Authors: Zachary Teed, Lahav Lipson, Jia Deng
What they did: Sparse patch-based deep visual odometry with differentiable bundle adjustment. Used by VehDyn to recover 6-DoF ego pose from generated video.

Title: DROID-SLAM: Deep Visual SLAM for Monocular, Stereo, and RGB-D Cameras
Authors: Zachary Teed, Jia Deng
What they did: Dense learned SLAM with recurrent updates and dense bundle adjustment. Candidate alternative to DPVO.

Title: MegaSaM: Accurate, Fast, and Robust Structure and Motion from Casual Dynamic Videos
Authors: Zhengqi Li, Richard Tucker, Forrester Cole, Qianqian Wang, Linyi Jin, Vickie Ye, Angjoo Kanazawa, Aleksander Holynski, Noah Snavely
Institution: Google DeepMind; UC Berkeley; University of Michigan
What they did: Camera and depth estimation for casual videos with dynamic content. Candidate relative-rotation and translation source.

Title: VGGT: Visual Geometry Grounded Transformer
Authors: Jianyuan Wang, Minghao Chen, Nikita Karaev, Andrea Vedaldi, Christian Rupprecht, David Novotny
What they did: Feed-forward transformer that predicts camera poses, depth and point maps from images. Representative of the VGGT-family route.

Title: GeoCalib: Learning Single-image Calibration with Geometric Optimization
Authors: Alexander Veicht, Paul-Edouard Sarlin, Philipp Lindenberger, Marc Pollefeys
Institution: ETH Zurich; Microsoft Mixed Reality & AI Lab
What they did: Single-image estimate of gravity direction (roll, pitch) and focal length via learned geometric optimization. Main absolute-tilt route.

Title: Perspective Fields for Single Image Camera Calibration
Authors: Linyi Jin, Jianming Zhang, Yannick Hold-Geoffroy, Oliver Wang, Kevin Matzen, Matthew Sticha, David F. Fouhey
What they did: Per-pixel up-vector and latitude fields from a single image, giving roll, pitch and field of view. Alternative gravity estimator.

Title: AnyCalib: On-Manifold Learning for Model-Agnostic Single-View Camera Calibration
Authors: Javier Tirado-Garín, Javier Civera
What they did: On-manifold single-image calibration for arbitrary lens models, relevant to fisheye footage. ID and authors need checking.

Title: MoGe-2: Accurate Monocular Geometry with Metric Scale and Sharp Details
Authors: Ruicheng Wang, Sicheng Xu, Yue Dong, Yu Deng, Jianfeng Xiang, Zelong Lv, Guangzhong Sun, Xin Tong, Jiaolong Yang
What they did: Recovers a metric-scale 3D point map from a single image. Candidate metric-scale source for implied tilt.

Title: RAFT: Recurrent All-Pairs Field Transforms for Optical Flow
Authors: Zachary Teed, Jia Deng
What they did: Optical flow network. NewtonRewards uses it as a velocity proxy; candidate for a flow-based tilt residual.

Title: The Blackbird Dataset: A Large-Scale Dataset for UAV Perception in Aggressive Flight
Authors: Amado Antonini, Winter Guerra, Varun Murali, Thomas Sayre-McCord, Sertac Karaman
What they did: 10+ hours of aggressive indoor quadrotor flight with mocap, IMU and motor RPM; images are rendered from real flight poses, so trajectories can be re-rendered with tilt altered.

Title: Race Against the Machine: a Fully-annotated, Open-design Dataset of Autonomous and Piloted High-speed Flight
Authors: Michael Bosello, Davide Aguiari, Yvo Keuter, Enrico Pallotta, Sara Kiade, Gyordan Caminati, Flavio Pinzarrone, Junaid Halepota, Jacopo Panerati, Giovanni Pau
Institution: Technology Innovation Institute (Autonomous Robotics Research Center); University of Bologna
What they did: Real fisheye video with mocap, IMU and motor thrust for autonomous and piloted high-speed flight (to ~21.8 m/s, above 7 g).

Title: Are We Ready for Autonomous Drone Racing? The UZH-FPV Drone Racing Dataset
Authors: Jeffrey Delmerico, Titus Cieslewski, Henri Rebecq, Matthias Faessler, Davide Scaramuzza
What they did: Indoor and outdoor aggressive FPV flight with event and grayscale fisheye cameras, IMU and laser-tracker ground truth.

Title: Mid-Air: A Multi-Modal Dataset for Extremely Low Altitude Drone Flights
Authors: Michael Fonder, Marc Van Droogenbroeck
What they did: Synthetic low-altitude drone flights with easy horizon cues and simulator pose and IMU.

Title: Wan: Open and Advanced Large-Scale Video Generative Models
Authors: Wan Team (Ang Wang, Baole Ai, Bin Wen et al.)
What they did: Open large-scale video generation models (Wan 2.1 / 2.2). Used for Image2World continuations and the scale trend in Phase 6.

Title: Cosmos World Foundation Model Platform for Physical AI
Authors: NVIDIA (Niket Agarwal, Arslan Ali, Maciej Bala et al.)
What they did: NVIDIA world foundation model platform. This is the original Cosmos paper; Cosmos-Predict2.5 (used in MotionScape) is a later release, so check for its own report.

Title: FlightDiffusion: Revolutionising Autonomous Drone Training with Diffusion Models Generating FPV Video
Authors: Valerii Serpiva, Artem Lykov, Faryal Batool, Vladislav Kozlovskiy, Miguel Altamirano Cabrera, Dzmitry Tsetserukou
Institution: Skolkovo Institute of Science and Technology (Intelligent Space Robotics Lab)
What they did: Diffusion framework that generates FPV video from a single frame to train autonomous drones. New find: FPV-style generation is exactly the footage our verifier targets.

Title: Beyond Visual Quality: Evaluating Physical Consistency under Ego-Motion with EgoGenEval
Authors: Yilin Long, Chenming Zhu, Zitang Gou, Jingli Lin, Tai Wang
Institution: Shanghai AI Laboratory; Fudan University; University of Hong Kong; Shanghai Jiao Tong University
What they did: Benchmark of physical consistency under ego-motion for visual generators. New find and the closest evaluation work to ours; read the abstract-level claim against the paper.

Title: Quantitative Video World Model Evaluation for Geometric-Consistency
Authors: Jiaxin Wu, Yihao Pi, Yinling Zhang, Yuheng Li, Xueyan Zou
Institution: Tsinghua University (IEI Lab); UW-Madison; Adobe Research
What they did: Quantitative evaluation of whether video world models produce physically plausible 3D structure and motion. New find; same measure-then-judge design as ours.

Title: GeoT2V-Bench: Benchmarking 3D Consistency in Text-to-Video Models via 3D Reconstruction
Authors: Chenrui Fan, Paolo Favaro
What they did: Scores 3D consistency of camera-prompted text-to-video outputs by reconstructing them in 3D. New find.

Title: Reference-Free Assessment of Physical Consistency in World Model-based Video Generation
Authors: Yun Oh, Sukmin Yun
What they did: Reference-free assessment of physical consistency in world-model video generation. New find.

Title: MotionPhys: Detecting AI-Generated Videos via Physical Consistency of Optical-Flow Trajectories
Authors: Haojin He, Hao Tan, Zichang Tan, Ajian Liu, Jun Wan
Institution: CAS Institute of Automation; UCAS; Sangfor Technologies
What they did: Detects AI-generated video from the physical consistency of optical-flow trajectories. New find; same test from a forensics angle, like PIVOT.

Title: FlowPilot: Real-Time World-Action Modeling for Agile UAV Navigation
Authors: Runqing Wang, Ding Yu, Pengyuan Min, Xinhong Zhang, Wei Xiao, Yu Hu, Jie Chen, Fu Zhang, Gang Wang
Institution: Beijing Institute of Technology; Shanghai Jiao Tong University; University of Hong Kong; Zhongguancun Academy
What they did: Real-time world-action modeling for agile UAV navigation. New find; only the title and author page were read.

Title: AirDreamer: Generalist Drone Navigation with World Models
Authors: Zian Liu, Andong Yang, Chunkai Yang, Ruidong An, Chao Gao, Guyue Zhou
Institution: Tsinghua University (Institute for AI Industry Research); Wuhan University
What they did: Generalist drone navigation with world models. New find; only the title and author page were read.

Title: WorldVLN: Autoregressive World Action Model for Aerial Vision-Language Navigation
Authors: Baining Zhao, Jiacheng Xu, Weicheng Feng, Xin Zhang, Zhaolu Wang, Haoyang Wang, Shilong Ji, Ziyou Wang, Jianjie Fang, Zhiheng Zheng, Weichen Zhang, Yu Shang, Wei Wu, Chen Gao, Xinlei Chen, Yong Li
Institution: Tsinghua University; Shandong University; Manifold AI; Beijing Institute of Technology; Northeastern University
What they did: Autoregressive world-action model for aerial vision-language navigation. New find; only the title and author page were read.

Title: Flatness-Preserving Residual Learning for Real-Time Tight Quadrotor Formation Flight
Authors: Pei-An Hsieh, Fengjun Yang, Nikolai Matni, M. Ani Hsieh
What they did: Learns downwash residual dynamics restricted to positions and velocities so the system stays differentially flat; thrust and angular velocity are then recovered algebraically from the flat outputs. Matches NMPC tracking at about 20x lower solve time on Crazyflies. Shows how to extend flatness reconstruction with a residual term (from the abstract and report).

Title: Online Learning and Control for Data-Augmented Quadrotor Model
Authors: Matej Smid, Jindrich Dunik
Institution: Czech Academy of Sciences (Institute of Computer Science); University of West Bohemia
What they did: Identifies quadrotor air drag online with a recursive Gaussian process on top of a physics model, and uses it in MPC (Gazebo). Gives the body-drag and rotor-drag equations. Useful for fitting the drag term in the implied-tilt equation.

Title: Vision-Based System Identification of a Quadrotor
Authors: Selim Ahmet Iz, Mustafa Unel
What they did: Grey-box and black-box system identification of a quadrotor from onboard vision and IMU data, with thrust and drag coefficient estimation and an LQR design. Lists the full equations of motion. Background for identifying thrust and drag coefficients.

Title: Vector Field Following for Quadrotors via Reduced Attitude Representations with Applications to Safety-Critical Control
Authors: Mohammad Mirtaba, Max H. Cohen
What they did: States that translational dynamics depend on attitude only through the thrust axis R*b3, and controls that thrust direction on the unit sphere. Directly supports using thrust direction (tilt) as the quantity to verify. Tested on Crazyflie.

Title: Reduced Order Observers for Monocular Visual Inertial Odometry
Authors: Amel Abi, Mouaad Boughellaba, Miaomiao Wang, Abdelhamid Tayebi
Institution: Lakehead University; Huazhong University of Science and Technology
What they did: Treats the body-frame gravity vector as a state in an LTV observer, recovering roll and pitch (not yaw) from monocular bearings and IMU. Gravity direction from vision is what our depicted-tilt side needs; this one needs an IMU, which generated video lacks.

Title: Geometric Inverse Flight Dynamics on SO(3) and Application to Tethered Fixed-Wing Aircraft
Authors: Antonio Franchi, Chiara Gabellieri
What they did: Coordinate-free closed-form map from a trajectory to attitude, angular velocity and thrust for fixed-wing aircraft; the abstract describes it as a building block for trajectory design and feasibility checks. Fixed-wing, so only the method carries over to quadrotors.

Title: Physics-Aware End-to-End Deep Reinforcement Learning for Quadcopter Control with Actuator Dynamics
Authors: Ya-Chia Shen, Woei-Leong Chan
What they did: DRL on a 12-state quadcopter model with thrust and torque allocation and first-order motor lag (time constant 0.076 s). Useful as a reference for actuator limits and lag, which bound how fast tilt can change.

Title: Safety-Critical Quadrotor Navigation Using Fourth-Order Control Barrier Functions with Full Nonlinear Quadrotor Dynamics
Authors: Yanze Liu, Yasar Idikut, Dhruv Madhusudan Agrawal, Wei Xiao, Guanrui Li
Institution: Worcester Polytechnic Institute; Nanyang Technological University
What they did: Safety filter on thrust and torque for the full 6-DoF model. States that a large commanded acceleration can push the vehicle to an attitude the low-level controller cannot track, which ties acceleration to tilt. Background.

Title: Coordinated Trajectory Control Algorithm for Quadcopter Motion along a Smooth Spatial Trajectory
Authors: S. A. Kim, A. A. Pyrkin, O. I. Borisov
What they did: Full quadcopter model with the roll and pitch dependence of acceleration written out, and an output-feedback law for following a spatial curve. Background on the acceleration-to-attitude relation.

Title: Direct Rotor Thrust Sensing and Feedback Control for Disturbance Rejection of Multirotors Using Load-cells
Authors: Peter Bohm, Michael Bruenig, Peyman Moghadam, Pauline E. I. Pounds
What they did: Measures rotor thrust with load cells to reject gusts, vortex ring state and ground effect, with the thrust model T = k_T w^2 minus an inflow term. Low priority; shows how far real thrust can deviate from the ideal model.

Title: NeuroBEM: Hybrid Aerodynamic Quadrotor Model
Authors: Leonard Bauersfeld, Elia Kaufmann, Philipp Foehn, Sihao Sun, Davide Scaramuzza
What they did: Hybrid blade-element and neural aerodynamic model; the abstract says aerodynamic effects, negligible at low speed, become the dominant model defect at high speed. Tells us when the drag-free tilt equation breaks down.

Title: Control of Complex Maneuvers for a Quadrotor UAV using Geometric Methods on SE(3)
Authors: Taeyoung Lee, Melvin Leok, N. Harris McClamroch
Institution: Affiliations not shown on the page I read (verify)
